summary: This is round-3/round-4 hardening of the interactive-session write-gate (a per-user bashrc/profile PATH-wrapper guard that blocks gh pr merge / git push to protected branches from interactive shells) plus its regression tests and a PROTOCOL_OWNER_AI.yaml article documenting it; the diff is additive (new PATH-search-based subcommand/global-flag scanning, a third task-registry cross-reference signal, expanded refspec/force-push parsing) and does not touch .github/workflows/**, migrations, schema, auth, payment, or .env paths, so tier1 classification is correct. I read the full shipped snippet and test suite and actually executed both tests/interactive_session_guard_test.sh (65 scenarios, all PASS, covering every claimed round-2/3/4 bypass closure including command-prefixed invocations, spoofed INVOCATION_ID, config-file/env-var cgroup-path overrides, force-push '+' refspecs, multi-refspec pushes, and global-flag-prefixed git/gh invocations) and python3 -m pytest tests/write_gate_test.py (1 passed), and validated the YAML with yaml.safe_load -- all green, not just a self-report. The code itself is sound: _interactive_guard_git_find_subcommand/_interactive_guard_gh_strip_globals correctly scan past documented global flags before subcommand detection, the three-signal is_real_worker_context check (INVOCATION_ID + kernel-read /proc/self/cgroup, hardcoded with no override + task.yaml cross-reference, also hardcoded with no override) closes the round-2/3 config-file and env-var spoofing bugs, and the multi-refspec/force-push-marker refspec parsing in _interactive_guard_git_push_verdict is correct. The documentation is unusually honest about what remains unsolved (same-account limitation, absolute-path/command -p bypass, finite version-tied global-flag allowlist, unresolved systemd-run impersonation question mitigated only by the task cross-reference) rather than overclaiming a hard security boundary, which is the right posture for what is explicitly a discipline/defense-in-depth tool, not a privilege boundary against the Owner's own account.
